_: Town building knobs (towns.gd reads them). castle: where a great house's castle may stand when the first, old search (eight headings on the square's ring, all dry) finds no plot: headings around, rings out from the square (0 is the old ring; -1 hugs the square), sizes tried in order, and the share of the plot's edge that may stand over water if the keep's middle is dry.
_density: density: how many houses a town raises (towns.gd _real_lots): base + per_size x its size, held between min and max, seat more at a great house's seat; crown: the crown's seat only (art target 01-town, plots shoulder to shoulder behind the square): extra houses.
_plots: A town is laid out in plots (town_plots.gd: roads first, burgage plots along them, a fenced yard behind each house). plots: set_back (street edge to a house front), yard (a yard's depth behind its house), gap (between two plots' houses), lane_every and lane_length (branch lanes along a road), lanes_per_size and lanes_most (lanes a town lays: (size - 2) x lanes_per_size, at most lanes_most), wander (how much a street bends on level ground), edge_more (how much further the plots run than the old palisade ring), square_ring (houses enclose the square between the roads in; ring_slide: a front turned away by a road in, a landmark or a stall slides on round the edge this far, game units, and is tried again; ring_first: the square's ring laid before the trades that stand off the plots, by the castle, the inn and the water, which took the band round the square first in round 4; square_roads: at most `most` roads run into the square, the realm's great roads first (01-town: the main street and a lane or two), the rest start at the first ring street, into_ring units inside it so they meet it, in a town with ring streets), fence (the yards' fence: a component in assets.json), yard_things (a yard's working thing in its back corner, each component by its chance: a woodshed, a pen), green (art target town-b: trees between the houses, gardens, hedges; each yard by its chance: tree, a fruit or shade tree at the back of the yard (assets.json town_tree); hedge, a hedge along its side fence (garden_hedge); flowers, a flower bed by the house's back door (garden_flowers); garden, its kitchen garden of vegetable rows (was 0.65); garden_depth, the bed's depth, fewest and most (was 0.3-0.42: with the bed holding a circle as wide as itself it took the whole yard, and batch 6's yards grew 3 trees for 61 houses); tree_ground, the ground a yard tree's trunk keeps others off (its crown overhangs the bed and the fence); square_trees, shade trees round the square's rim before the house fronts (research rule 8: a town centre's trees cluster at its square); edge_trees: trees just outside the town's edge, one per that many units of it), near (a house stands only within this of something already standing, the square, the castle, a landmark or a house, so a town grows out from its heart with one edge and no house alone on the fields; 0 turns it off); ring_wobble: how far a ring street wanders in and out of its circle (0.35 unset; the crown's 0.1, with wander 0.06, round 6: straight streets so its houses stand in rows facing them). crown: the crown's seat's own (art target 01-town: narrow, deep plots shoulder to shoulder), and extra, how many more houses it raises on plots. rings: ring streets round the square, each this far out from its edge (game units; art target town-b, Manor Lords: streets circling the market behind its first row), arcs between the castle, the landmarks and the water, lined with houses on both sides; none elsewhere. The crown's seat (round 2 against 01-town: houses loose on grass; now yard 0.4 (was 0.55), gap 0.01 (was 0.02), extra 48 (was 40), so the rows stand back to back; rings [2.6, 4.8] tried in round 3 cut fewer plots, 80 not 92, and stood fewer houses, so back to): rings [2.8, 5.2], edge_more 2.4 (was 1.6), lanes_most 4 (was 14: twelve lanes criss-crossing three roads cut 27 plots and stood 16 houses in batch 6). seat: a great house's seat's own (Goldrock; towns.gd town_rank), town: a market town's (at least min_size), on top of plots as crown's is: every large town rings its square with streets and packs its plots by its size (headless probe, flat land, three roads: a seat 9-14 houses before, 51-57 after; a size 5-6 town 20-23 before, 35-37 after).

royal_works._: The King's own works (the bridge's royalWorks, a building site in a crown town: town_life.gd _construction): turn, radians from the far side of the town the town view looks across toward the frame's right (negative: its left), the side the site is tried first; pennant, the crown's pennant's height over the scaffold (world units).

manor._: A small seat (towns.gd town_rank manor: a house's seat or a bannerman's town no bigger than max_size, a vassal's new seat): its manor house in its walled garden (trades.list house_manor ranks) and a hamlet of houses round it; no castle, no market square; landmarks, those on its green (the church: its chapel; a town's are its tavern, hall and church), the manor house heading it (trades.list where_by_rank).

_tiers: tiers (town_tiers.gd decides each house): ladder, the house components poorest first (hovel, cottage, townhouse, merchant, burgher, manor: assets.json); corner, the component a corner plot may take (corner_share of the time), a rung up (corner_up). wealth: per zone the weight of each rung, near the square (near) and at the edge (far), eased between: square (the ring facing the square: mostly narrow townhouses, 01-town's gabled fronts shoulder to shoulder; round 5, 0.15/0.45/0.32/0.08 stood 3 wide merchants' and burghers' fronts on the rim the castle and three roads leave), main (the main streets), lane (the lanes). min_size: the smallest town each rung stands in (a seat counts seat_size bigger); manor_most: manors a town may raise on its plots (0: the manor is a trade, walled with its garden past the edge; trades.list house_manor). No two neighbours on a street are the same model.

fronts._: The houses a rank raises in a zone in place of the kit tiers (town_tiers.gd front_set; docs/research/meshy-square-set.md, Mac: 'I still don't see the meshy stuff integrated'): per rank, zones (square: facing the square; main: along a main street; lane: the back streets, round 12's hero shot showed their kit houses behind the square) and map, the kit house component a tier picked -> the component standing in its place (square_cottage, square_townhouse, square_merchant: the Meshy square set, meshy.json sq_*). Elsewhere the kit's tiers stand.

map_seat._: A house seat on the realm map (map_seat.gd, town_banners.gd map_seat; docs/art/target/02-realm.jpg: a castle and a tall banner per seat): the castle set's keep `keep` world units tall with the house's standard `standard` tall over it, shown from `from` away (map zoom), grown with the camera's distance past `ref`, at most `most` times (Total War's campaign map).

square._cover: cover_share: the coverage rule (town_scenes.gd cover_people, anchors.open cover): no stretch of the square's open setts nobody stands within near_m of may be bigger than this share of its open setts: 01-town's (targets.largest_empty_m2, 30 m2, over its about 470 m2 of open setts; Kingsmere's about 1290 m2 make it about 83 m2). Staging lays standing people one by one, farthest from everyone, inside the square's census budget and never more than cover_most (Mac: round 11's open court, r11 c01, wins over full coverage; tools/square_open_probe.gd).
square._: What a lived-in square measures (autoplay squarelife Town secs, its CHECK square life line, a measuring tool only: town_life drives the numbers). targets: counted by eye in docs/art/target/01-town.jpg, its cobbled square between the stalls, the well, the forge and the castle steps (estimates, Mac's approved concept): people in it, people per 100 m2 of open paving (the setts less what stands on them), the share standing (not walking), the share of people alone, in 2-4 and in 5+ (within near_m of each other), the largest stretch of open paving no one stands within near_m of (m2, at most), and the share within near_m of a stall, the well, the statue or a doorstep. The casebook's Living towns cases (docs: https://claude.ai/artifact/PzdycNn8Wj2xdTp8AX7AYK): idle_crowd, the crowd is the census (Stronghold: spare hands standing about together in one place; the largest knot of standing people, a 5+ knot by a stall in 01-town); trodden, desire paths (Foundation: people keep to the same ways; the share of walking on the busiest fifth of the open setts, about 0.2 if they wander at random).

_trades: trades (town_trades.gd plans, towns.gd stands them; the land goes to them before the houses): list, in the order they claim land; each stands when the town has one of its needs (the bridge's buildings), or is at least min_size, or (seat) is a great house's seat. where: main (a plot on a main street, t: its window from the square (0) to the edge (1)), lane (a plot on a lane), gate (a main-street plot toward the edge, by the road out), inn (beside the inn on the square, turned along its edge), castle (beside the castle, or the square where there is none), water (on the shore, the nearest dry flat ground to water), high (the highest open ground just past the edge), edge (just past the edge by a main road, toward the fields), downstream (on the shore, the lowest ground past the edge). trade_art: kit (the trades raised from the kit or the catalogue's models) or ai (the image-to-3D models in assets.json ai lists); --trade_art=ai for one run.
_market: stalls_most: the most stalls a square holds, stall_gap: the room between neighbouring stalls as a share of a stall's width (towns.gd lay_stalls). The crown's square is a packed market again (Mac, 2026-11-12: 'round 11 looks much better than round 15', 'big square, 16 stalls', and what he likes in it: 'the level of detail, the openness'; casebook 'The market is a place'): square_r 2.1, round 11's, its house fronts at round 11's distance (7a8153dd's 1.1 held 6 stalls at most with lanes), 15-18 Meshy stalls in two rows (0.9 of the square over 158 degrees either side of the market's middle, 0.62 over 140), half a stall apart, running round toward the gate with the way in and the King's statue kept clear; the wagon draws up at the inner row's end away from the statue (towns.gd wagon_spot). realm/tools/square_density_probe.gd guards it: round 11's size, at least its 16 stalls and 226 goods, 55% of the square open ground, 1.2 m between stalls, 2 m round the well, the statue and the gate's way clear. lane_m, walk_m, gate_way_m: the square's walk rules in metres (between two things a buyer or a cart passes, round the well's rim, either side of the way to the castle gate), read by towns.gd strew_spots and square_density_probe. strew: the third toward the gate filled with small things (GoC on round 16, bare paving there; round 11's crates, benches, barrels and sacks): a bench (anchor) with goods (2-3) stacked at each end, on rings (shares of the square) every step degrees within third degrees either side of the gate's way, at most most, each reach (game units) round, where it clears the walk rules (towns.gd strew_spots). stall_posts: a lantern on its post at the front corner of every other stall (the rest keep their ground lantern). smithy: the crown's smithy on the square's edge (trades.list forge where_by_rank crown square), banner [across, up, width, height] metres on its front, barrel and rack [across, out] metres from its front. square_r_grown (the crown's: 2.1, was square_r 1.6; round 6, its rim had room for 3 fronts): the square's radius, game units. centre: the square's centrepiece at its heart in the well's stead, a component (assets.json well: the Meshy square set's roofed draw well, a seat's heart since round 11 dropped the kit's grey fountain; square_statue: the set's King on his plinth, beside the crown's well, art target 01-town), none: the draw well off the heart, as before. market.seat and market.town: a great house's seat's and a market town's square and market (square_r, stalls_more, goods, piles, as the crown's; towns.gd by the town's rank). market.crown: the crown's seat's market at midday (art target 01-town: some twenty at work round the square; town-b: a great paved square full of stalls and goods). square_r: its square's half-width (game units; 1.25 at other seats, was 1.25 here); goods: the heaps at each stall's ends, fewest and most (1-3 elsewhere); piles: how many house fronts round the square take a pile of the market's goods, against the wall beside the door (towns.gd _square_piles; Anno 1800's and Manor Lords' markets: stock stacked where it's sold, never strewn in the walk; a stall's own goods are squared piles at its ends); stalls_more (stalls past a seat's three, and the Marketplace's two; the kit's stalls are a third as wide as the pack's, so more stand), rows (the stalls in rows facing the square's heart: each row's radius as a share of square_r and its share of the stalls, outer first; one row at 0.8 elsewhere), span (how far either side of the market's middle a row runs, degrees: a row stops when full, so the pack's wide stalls stand fewer), buyers (each stall's buyers, fewest and most; 1-2 elsewhere), smith (a smith at his anvil), carts (carters selling from a cart), porters (porters at the stalls' ends), rooms (how many each of its places holds: market, well, tavern, sept), out_most (the most of its people out by day; 40 elsewhere), farmers_to_market (the share of would-be farmers who keep a city trade at the market instead). counter: a stall's counter piled with its wares (comp: the component they come from, assets.json stall_wares: apples, melons, carrots, pots and sacks from the market pack, crates and a barrel of apples from the kit; height and depth out as shares of the stall's width, count low and high, scale of each, span along the counter); well_too: the roofed draw well beside a centrepiece (the crown's statue), well_at its distance from the heart as a share of the square's radius.
_paving: paving (art target town-b: cobbles over the square and the main streets): texture (the look audit's painted setts, assets/ground/painted_v2/setts.png, a stone about 25 cm, 2.5 m a tile; graded to 01-town's grey-beige worn cobbles with magick -modulate 112,45,100 after group render g1 read them orange-terracotta brick: mean 0.61, 0.54, 0.48, was 0.64, 0.46, 0.34), tint (a multiply, warm grey-beige), tile (game units one copy of the stone covers: 0.32; stones_across, the setts across one copy of the texture: 10 in the painted setts (painted_v2/setts.png, about 2.5 m a tile), so a sett is tile / M / stones_across = 0.27 m, a sixth of a person as in 01-town: art step 6, docs/art/STANDARDS.md section 2; it was cobbles-painted.jpg at 0.3, about 5 across, a 0.48 m sett that swamped the crowd. The sheet carries the smaller setts, not a smaller tile: at tile 0.16 the long streets hit terrain.tiled's 64-copy cap and the decal textures outgrew the GPU ('Texture dimensions exceed device maximum', a blank frame); tools/town_look_probe.gd checks it), so a stone shows about 17 px from the town view and the square reads as round 11's grey setts (Mac's pick), not sand; the look audit paints it (painted_v2/setts.png), still_probe.py setts judges the frame), square (the square's paving across, as a multiple of its half-width: 2 reaches its edge, more runs under the house fronts), square_aspect (its depth as a share of its width), streets (the share of each main street, from the square out, laid with setts: crown the crown's seat, seat a great house's seat, town any other), width (a paved street's width as a share of the street's earth).
_lanes: lanes (paved: the ranks whose back lanes are laid in the paving's setts too, with straight-ish kerbs: crown, art target 01-town; research rule 16: dirt lanes 4-5 m with soft edges; the main and ring streets keep their earth and, by rank, their cobbles, paving): the back lanes off the main streets as trodden earth. ground: worn into the land itself where it is Terrain3D's (the square's mud stamped along the lane every `stamp` units, blending into the grass at its edge); otherwise, or with ground false, a decal of `texture` with soft frayed verges and no ruts, tinted `tint`. width: the lane's worn width as a share of a street's (0.34 units, about 2.8 m).
_props: props.sink: how far a prop on the square (stall, wagon, barrels, crates, the well) sits into the ground below the lowest of its middle and four corners (game units; 0.006 is about 5 cm), so nothing hangs over a slope.
_edge: edge (art target town-a/b: the town in its fields): mill_wheat, wheat fields laid round each windmill that stood (how many); orchards, how many orchards by the town's rank (crown, seat, town, village), by the roads out just past the edge; orchard: each one's rows and columns of trees (fewest, most), their spacing (game units; 0.55 is about 4.5 m) and size (a share of assets.json orchard_tree's height).
_farms: farms.fieldRise: the most a farmstead's field's ground may rise across it (game units, about 3 m); steeper and the field is not laid (its paint was cut off in a triangle on a slope).

fieldwork._: Sowing and harvest take the town to its fields (the casebook, Living towns): in these seasons (the realm's, bridge date) a town is in the fields state (town_life.gd fields_season): the square thins (town_scenes.json the rows' fields numbers) and to_fields of its market-goers, idlers and crafters walk out to work a strip instead (villagers.gd, as their crowd is made).

wet._: Rain drives folk indoors (Foundation's and Banished's rain): in this weather (the realm's, bridge weather.js) a town is in the wet state (town_life.gd wet): the square thins (town_scenes.json the rows' wet numbers) and those out walk hurry times faster (villagers.gd).

royal_funeral._: The King dead (bridge royals.js line: died, not abdicated): for this many seasons his seat buries him (awareness.gd royal_funeral; town_scenes.json royal_funeral row).

_season_states: season_states: the state a season puts every town in (town_life.gd _states): autumn's stores (the harvest carted in and carried to the granary: town_scenes.json stores row, the cart row's stores, works.json weights.stores) and winter's rations and winter itself (the winter row's firewood by the doors, every hearth lit: hearths.json winter; a queue at the granary: works.json counts.granary_queue.rations, weights.rations).

promise._: The King's word heard in a town (bridge promises.js): for this many seasons after a promise to it is kept or broken it shows (awareness.gd promise_kept, promise_broken; town_scenes.json the promise rows): kept, a knot cheering at the crier and the bell's peal; broken, sullen knots and scrawls on its walls (town_dress/scrawl.gd: how many, how far out in square radii, the words, their size and colour).

plague._: A plague town (the town scope's plague, bridge view.js): indoors, the share of its folk who keep to their houses while it lasts (villagers.gd); crosses, how many doors round the square are marked with the red cross (town_dress/plague_doors.gd), within so many square radii, the cross's colour and size.

rebuilding._: A sacked town rebuilding (works.gd rebuilding: the town scope's burnt share, bridge damage.js, falling a step each season as its folk rebuild; fire.gd mends each shell as it does): from, the burnt share past which its survivors are seen at work (town_scenes.json rebuilding row, town_dress/rebuild.gd).

royal_rest._: How long the King's rest is seen at his seat (awareness.gd _king_rests; bridge royals.js rest): seasons after he took it, his feast on the square, the faithful praying at the sept for his pilgrimage.

raid._: A town under raid (awareness.gd raid: the realm's raids slice, bridge raids.js, its raiders within near tiles of the town): its folk run and go indoors within indoors seconds (villagers.gd), the square empties (town_scenes.json director.square_off), the sept's bell rings the alarm and burn of its outer houses catch (town_scenes.json raid row, town_dress/raid.gd).

grow._: A town that grew is seen growing (towns.gd _grow): sites, at most this many of its new buildings rise as building sites at once (town_life.raise_site); the rest stand at once; seasons, how many seasons a new house takes to rise.

town_wall._: The town's stone wall round its edge in place of the palisade, for a town holding Freeciv's City Walls or whose wall the damage fact shows worn (towns.gd _town_wall, _holds_wall; castle_builder.gd town_wall: the castle's curtain, stone, slits and merlons; 01-town's town wall in the distance with towers and a gate): out, game units out from the plots' edge; storeys, its height (3 m each); turn_deg, a tower where the line turns more than this; gate_half_m, the gap each gatehouse (where a main road runs out) takes either side.

nav._: What stands in a town's way, read off its geometry (nav_ground.gd; town_nav.gd bakes the walk map from it). slice: how high above a thing's foot it is taken (game units; a tree's trunk, not its crown); tall: lower than this is walked over (flowers, pebbles); off_ground: a thing whose foot is this far above the ground is hung up (apples, banners) and left out; least: smaller outlines are dropped; big: a foot larger than this (a town wall's ring as one mesh) is traced as cells instead; cell: those cells' size; skip_names: nodes walked into by those who work them (fields, beds); skip_groups: what moves. open_cost: what open ground costs a walker against a street (town_nav.gd): people keep to the streets but cross a green between two neighbouring lanes rather than all funnel through the square. wide: how far a horse's and a cart's walk map keeps from anything standing (game units, about 0.75 m: half a wagon's width; town_nav.gd map_for wide, a person's keeps AGENT 0.035), so a cart never squeezes between two benches a man can pass.

yield._: A horse or a cart waits while any body stands on the arc it is about to drive (mover.gd _in_the_way): ahead, how far along it looks (game units); side, how far past its own half-width (wide); wait_max, seconds it (and a road party's head) waits before it goes round, then gives up.
